Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

Looking at the examples, I notice some patterns:

**Example 1 (2025-07-01):**
- History: Price started at 72.74 and generally moved downward to 68.97
- Sentiment: Mostly 0.00 except early on (0.33, -0.33, 0.67)
- Model forecast: Starts at 70.63, gradually increasing to ~75.79
- True outcome: Starts at 70.58, gradually increasing to ~75.37

The model seems to be forecasting slightly too high in the early part but catches up. Let me look more carefully...

Actually, let me re-examine. In Example 1:
- At day 1, model forecasts 70.63 vs true 70.58 (off by +0.05)
- At day 5, model forecasts 72.48 vs true 71.20 (off by +1.28)
- At day 10, model forecasts 72.12 vs true 70.42 (off by +1.70)
- At day 15, model forecasts 70.55 vs true 69.36 (off by +1.19)
- At day 20, model forecasts 71.43 vs true 70.65 (off by +0.78)
- At day 25, model forecasts 73.37 vs true 71.59 (off by +1.78)
- At day 30, model forecasts 75.79 vs true 73.21 (off by +2.58)

The model consistently forecasts about 1-2.5 points too high, especially in the middle horizon (days 5-25).
